name: Sorrel
grown_as: Common or garden sorrel, a perennial picked for its sharp, lemony leaves. ⚠️ CHECK which plant is meant: William's records list two sorrels that are other species, 'Volare' (given as Rumex patientia, patience dock: large, long, lance-shaped leaves, 1 m or more) and 'Red Lava' (Rumex sanguineus, bloody dock: oblong green leaves with deep red veins). Drawn as common sorrel, which looks unlike either.
habit: A leafy clump 20 to 40 cm tall from a short rootstock. In early summer slender, upright, little-leaved flowering stems 50 to 100 cm, turning red.

leaf.arrangement: A loose rosette from the base; a few alternate leaves on the flowering stem
leaf.outline: Oblong to arrow-shaped, 7 to 15 cm long, two to four times as long as wide
leaf.base: Arrow-shaped: two pointed lobes pointing backwards, down along the stalk, not out to the sides
leaf.margin: Smooth, no teeth, sometimes slightly wavy
leaf.veins: A midrib and a net of fine side veins, not prominent
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless, slightly fleshy, matt to faintly shiny
leaf.stalk: Rosette leaves on long stalks, as long as the blade or longer; upper stem leaves stalkless and clasping, with a thin papery sheath round the stem where the stalk joins
leaf.colour: Mid green, sometimes flushed red, especially in winter

flower.form: Tiny flowers without petals, in whorled clusters along slender branched spikes; male and female flowers on separate plants
flower.colour: Green flushed red, the whole spike turning rusty red
flower.centre: Male flowers: six yellowish stamens; female flowers: tufted red feathery stigmas
flower.carried: In loose upright, branched, leafless spikes at the top of the stem, the flowers in small spaced whorls

fruit: Three inner tepals grow into rounded papery wings 3 to 4 mm round a three-sided, glossy dark brown nut about 2 mm, each wing with a tiny wart at its base. The spikes go from red to rusty brown.
seedling: Two narrow oblong-oval seed leaves on short stalks, then small rounded to oval true leaves; the arrow-shaped base appears on later leaves.
winter: A small low rosette of a few leaves, often reddened, or bare crown in hard winters.

leaf: an oblong leaf with an arrow-shaped base
the two base lobes pointing back down along the stalk
smooth edges and a long stalk
bloom: in small spaced whorls along a slender spike
seed: a small three-sided glossy dark brown nut
seedling: the first true leaves rounded on stalks
young: a clump of long-stalked oblong leaves with arrow-shaped bases
crop: a leafy clump of arrow-based oblong leaves on long stalks
flower: slender upright red-tinged spikes rising above the leaf clump
few small clasping leaves on the flowering stem
seedhead: rusty red to brown branched spikes crowded with small papery fruits
dormant: a small low rosette of a few leaves, some reddened
low to the soil, no stems

look_alikes: Sheep's sorrel (Rumex acetosella) is smaller, with base lobes spreading out to the sides. French sorrel (Rumex scutatus) has shield-shaped grey-green leaves. Docks have larger leaves without the arrow base. Take care with lords-and-ladies (Arum maculatum, poisonous): its glossy arrow-shaped leaf has a net of veins and lobes that spread out and down.
